chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you rise from your sleep at night, say: 'All praise is for Allah Who returned my soul to me, so that I may praise Him and worship Him.'

And when you hear the voice of the rooster, say: 'Glorious, Holy is the Lord of the Angels and the Spirit. Your mercy precedes Your anger. There is no god except You, Alone. I have done evil and been unjust to myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.'

And when you stand, look towards the horizons of the sky and say: 'O Allah! Neither does a dark night hide from You, nor a sky with constellations, nor an earth with flatness, nor darkness upon darkness, nor a deep sea where one wave precedes another. From among Your creatures, You know the betrayal of the eyes and what the chests conceal. The stars have set and the eyes have slept, yet You are the Living, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes You. Glorious is my Lord, Lord of the worlds, and God of the Messengers. And all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: the betrayal of the eyes (glances that deceive)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications to recite when waking up for night prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the spiritual protocol for waking for Tahajjud, emphasizing the transition from sleep to worship through specific dhikrs and a contemplative dua. It highlights the Imam's instruction to observe the night sky, linking the physical signs of creation (stars, earth, sea) with Allah's eternal attributes of knowledge and power, a practice rooted in Shia tradition to deepen focus before standing for prayer.
